## Hypotheses (pre-registered branches)
H1 matrices are close to low-rank (rank by the stated estimator). H2 designed selection beats random-k with the same inference for k below ~r and the gap closes afterwards. H3 measured curve follows T1/T2 on synthetic data (with estimation term) and on real data up to the reported misfit. H4 adaptivity gains only under misspecification. H5 conclusions weaken, quantifiably, under extrapolation, sparsity, small M, saturation, granularity.
**Negative branch (stated now):** if S0+P5 matches S6+P5 beyond very small k, the main finding is "selection matters only for k ≲ r, needed k ≈ r+Δ, random-k suffices", with T1/T2 explaining why. If the real-matrix knee/1/k predictions fail, the misfit decomposition is the finding.

## Evaluation protocol
- **Matrix definition (fixed before running):** one benchmark = one task (languages/subsets averaged), the main score of the benchmark's standard split, one revision per model by a rule fixed beforehand; task versions not mixed. Coarser (task-type) and finer (language-level) granularity as a data-condition sweep: N and thus "k ≪ N" depends on it. A coverage-filter table is mandatory.
- **Gate:** report the post-filter shape first. If it has fewer than roughly ≥100 models × ≥30 tasks with run sets large enough to choose k ≥ 8 from, narrow the claims rather than weaken the filter.
- **Holdout:** group-wise (org/family stem, after dedup) is primary; temporal/strength split second primary; plain leave-one-model-out only as sensitivity. Everything (standardisation, factor fit, hyperparameters, selection) fit on training models only; held-out run set restricted to benchmarks the model has; error on its remaining observed cells. Missingness is MNAR (authors report chosen tasks): stated as a limitation.
- **Primary contrast (fixed):** S6+P5 vs S0+P5 at k ∈ {1,2,3,5,8,12,20}, paired over held-out models, bootstrap CI over models/groups; gain judged against the draw-to-draw spread of random-k. All else secondary with multiplicity stated. Report k=1,2,3 vs the mean-offset (general-factor) baseline explicitly.
- **Metrics:** standardised RMSE; MAE in raw points; error vs typical gap between adjacent leaderboard models; per-model Spearman; rank agreement among strong models; per-benchmark error. Floors: "residual floor", "all-others floor".
- **Equal terms:** all baselines' hyperparameters tuned by the same inner CV on training models.
- **Synthetic:** known rank/noise; generated from the model, then a misspecification ladder (saturating link, heavy tails, heteroscedastic noise near ceiling, correlated residuals within task type, decaying spectrum), estimated-parameter version with M varied.

shown.message:
I accepted the three re-review items and put them into Brief rev. 3 (wiki commit 0fda4b8). I ran no experiments, so nothing is tested yet.

- **k grid:** the grid is tied to the realised N. The headline statements use k ≤ ⌊N/3⌋, with k/N on the axis, and larger k appears only as a labelled supplement. k counts benchmarks inside the held-out model's own run set. Models whose run set is smaller than k are excluded at that k, and the number excluded is reported per k. The headline curve is also computed on the fixed subset of models that have at least k_max run cells. A matrix with N < 60 supports the headline only up to about N/3, and the title and abstract scope is narrowed to match.
- **Equivalence margin:** the margin δ is the smaller of half the median adjacent-model gap and 25% of the all-others-floor RMSE, computed from training data. "Random-k matches design" needs the group-bootstrap 90% CI of the paired difference to lie within ±δ. "Design helps" needs the CI to lie beyond +δ. Anything between is reported as undecided.
- **k\* check:** the predicted k*(ε) is compared with the empirical k* for ε = δ and 2δ. If they disagree, the misfit decomposition becomes the finding.
- **Held-out groups:** the number of held-out groups is reported with every CI. Below about 20 groups, the CIs are stated as indicative and the temporal split carries the headline.
- **Pre-registration:** I opened issue #2 in `experiment-repo` asking it to write down the cell, revision, dedup and group rules, the realised post-filter shape and the numeric δ, with a commit and date, before any result is computed. The same issue asks it to name any baseline that can't be run as published.

I commented on my commitment issue #2 and on review issue #3. #2 stays open until the Outline and the plan review land.
